text:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: node-gpu-12 ephemeral-storage > 95% (inodes 99%). Multiple serve-runtime pods evicted in the last 2m. Affected deployment: conv-serve-prod. Auto-alerting paging oncall.

alex: seeing a spike in 502s from the hosted API? any customer reports yet?

sre-oncall: yep, graphs show error-rate up ~4% for text-generation across us-west-2. I'm looking at node events now.

priya: kubelet events from node-gpu-12:
```
Warning  Evicted  1m   kubelet    Pod ephemeral local storage eviction
Warning  OOMKilled  58s  kubelet   Container runtime crashed
```
Modelcache pod (conv-serve-7fdc) got evicted, then restarted and failed to init.

miguel: grabbed logs from the restarted pod, modelcache errors: `mmap failed: ENOSPC` and a bunch of "No space left on device" during checkpoint write.

alex: that sounds like inode exhaustion rather than raw bytes. any clues on what created so many files?

sre-oncall: `du -sh /tmp/modelcache && find /tmp/modelcache -type f | wc -l` shows `/tmp/modelcache 1.2G` but `4,120,033` files. checkpoints are sharded tiny files.

priya: oh wow. a bug in the new checkpoint streamer created a tmp file per shard and didn't rotate. That would create millions of tiny files and blow inodes.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-02-28T03:14:22 conv-checkpoint-streamer@v2 promoted to prod (rollout 100%).

miguel: timeline matches. rollout ~03:14, inode usage climbs, first pod evicted ~03:27.

sre-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-gpu-12 to stop new pods landing 2) scale conv-serve-prod down from 12 -> 8 replicas to give breathing room 3) schedule cleanup on node to remove orphaned tmp shards 4) route traffic to canary region/fallback model for critical customers.

emma: I'm taking handoff if this lasts. quick ask: can we safely delete `*/tmp/checkpoint_shard_*.tmp` files on the host? any consumer might be mid-write.

miguel: safe-ish — the streamer app writes `.tmp` then renames. if we remove `.tmp` files older than 5m we should be ok. command I ran locally:
```
ssh node-gpu-12
sudo find /tmp/modelcache -type f -name "*.tmp" -mmin +5 -delete
```
Use caution. I'll run dry-run first:
```
sudo find /tmp/modelcache -type f -name "*.tmp" -mmin +5 -print | head
```

sre-oncall: running dry-run now, looks like ~2.6M .tmp files older than 5m. that's the bulk.

alex: CS — do we have customers affected with SLAs? cs-rep please chime in.

cs-rep: two mid-market customers (acme-analytics, herochat) reported degraded response times. no major revenue customers on Dedicated in this node group. I'll open incident page and ping them.

priya: I've cordoned node-gpu-12 and started the delete job (non-blocking, using -mmin +5). Monitoring inode usage dropping.

sre-oncall: inode usage dropping from 99% -> 64% over 6m after cleanup. restarting evicted pods now.

miguel: restarted conv-serve pods. modelcache now starts clean, no ENOSPC in logs. CUDA init errors we saw were cascade from container restarts, should be fine now.

deploy-bot: Rollback option: promote conv-checkpoint-streamer@v1 if any regression. would you like me to queue rollback?

priya: hold rollback for now unless we see regenerating tmp files. leave streamer v2 but add a quick guard: limit open shard writes. I'll open emergency PR to change tmp naming and cleanup logic.

sre-oncall: customer impact summary (initial): ~4% error spike for 12m window, ~0.7% total requests returned 502. Two customer support tickets opened, CS notified. No data loss reported. Root cause: new checkpoint streamer leaking millions of .tmp shard files -> inode exhaustion -> kubelet eviction -> container restarts -> transient CUDA init failures.

emma: taking oncall for followup. I'll monitor for 2 hours, coordinate rollback if tmp file count increases. Assigning follow-up tasks: MIGUEL -> postmortem logs and `find` output; PRIYA -> emergency PR and hotfix; ALEX -> confirm no other nodes with same issue; CS-REP -> customer comms.

sre-oncall: leaving note: if disk/inode usage rises again, execute rollback command (deploy-bot):
```
deploy-bot rollback conv-checkpoint-streamer v1 --reason "inode exhaustion in prod"
```

cs-rep: customers informed: sent initial P0 note to acme-analytics and herochat, keeping them updated.

emma: :wave: summarizing handoff: cordoned node, cleaned ~2.6M tmp files, scaled down conv-serve briefly, restarted pods, error rate normalized. watching for recurrence. tagging postmortem and follow-up tasks.

monitoring-bot: Incident updated: status -> mitigated. next steps: postmortem assignment and deploy hotfix."
